question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}\frac{3-\sqrt{3x}}{x-3} & =\frac{3-\sqrt{3(3)}}{3-3}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the numerator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}\frac{3-\sqrt{3x}}{x-3} & ={lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}\frac{(3-\sqrt{3x})(3+\sqrt{3x})}{(x-3)(3+\sqrt{3x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}\frac{{3}^{2}-{(\sqrt{3x})}^{2}}{(x-3)(3+\sqrt{3x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}\frac{9-3x}{(x-3)(3+\sqrt{3x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}\frac{-3(x-3)}{(x-3)(3+\sqrt{3x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {3}^{-}}\frac{-3}{3+\sqrt{3x}} \\  & =\frac{-3}{3+\sqrt{3\cdot 3}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
